writeup.headline: Shopify rates Buy on fast growth, net cash and firm trend, but sits just 2 points above Hold.
writeup.thesis: Shopify scores 66, a Buy, carried by growth (81), a perfect balance sheet score (100) and a solid trend (73). Revenue is expanding quickly, with TTM revenue growth of 32.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 33.7% year on year, though growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 68 on a 17.7% FCF margin, a 13.9% operating margin and diluted share count down 0.8% year on year, and the company holds net cash with no debt. The main drag is valuation at 32: in absolute terms the multiples are high, at 16.2x sales, 91.5x FCF and 114.0x EV/EBIT, with the FCF yield 3.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, even though the stock screens as cheap against its own history. News is mildly positive (59), helped by broker price-target raises and Google's Universal Cart launch on a protocol Shopify co-developed.
key_risks: High absolute valuation (91.5x FCF, 114.0x EV/EBIT) leaves little room for a growth disappointment.
Q3 results on Nov 3 could reset expectations, especially after pre-earnings target raises.
Growing agentic-commerce competition from Amazon, OpenAI and Meta.
Ongoing Sezzle antitrust and Briskin privacy cases.
Longer-term momentum is weak, with shares down 16.7% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago.
what_would_change: A drop of just 2 points would move the rating to Hold, for example from slower growth or a weaker trend after Q3.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 14 more points, most plausibly from a better valuation score or stronger quality margins.
A guidance cut or analyst downgrades around the Nov 3 report would pull the news risk score down.
Further growth deceleration would erode the growth factor, the largest positive contributor.
